newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia cuts overseas radio broadcaster budget.
newsitem.headline: Australia cuts overseas radio broadcaster budget.

text.p: Australia on Tuesday slashed the operations of its international state-owned radio broadcaster, Radio Australia, cutting funds by two-thirds and scrapping several regional language services, Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio reported.

The cabinet decided not to abolish the service, as originally expected, but chose to cut funding to about A$7 million (US$5.4 million) from more than A$23 million, said the corporation, which runs Radio Australia.
Radio Australia broadcasts in Cantonese, French, Khmer, Mandarin, Thai and Vietnamese will be axed.
Indonesian language services may also be halted.
Radio Australia broadcasts on shortwave and via satellite and has millions of listeners throughout the region.
The corporation reported that South Pacific services would remain.
Australia's year-old conservative Liberal-National government is cutting government spending to achieve a balanced budget in the fiscal year to June 30, 1999.
